author: BrentDesk Staff
headline: Mobedex covers furniture, flooring and smart home technology in Jeddah
deck: Furniture, doors, flooring and smart home technology sell into a refurbishment market considerably less cyclical than construction.
excerpt: Mobedex runs concurrently with JIBEX in Jeddah covering furniture, doors, flooring and smart home technology, serving a refurbishment market alongside new build.
content:
Mobedex runs alongside JIBEX at the Jeddah Centre for Exhibitions and Events from 15 to 17 September, covering furniture, paints, doors and windows, hotel equipment, flooring, smart home technology, curtains and home textiles.

The market it addresses is substantial and receives less attention than it merits. Jeddah's residential stock is large and long-established, and the interiors categories Mobedex covers are bought both for new construction and for refurbishment — with the second market considerably less cyclical than the first.

That refurbishment channel deserves more prominence in Saudi construction coverage than it usually gets. Reporting concentrates, reasonably, on new build: giga-projects, residential programmes, industrial capacity. But a housing stock of Saudi Arabia's size generates continuous demand for replacement kitchens, bathrooms, flooring and joinery, and that demand is served by small contractors buying from distributors rather than by main contractors buying on specification. It is a different channel with different products, different margins and a different sales cycle.

It is also more resilient. New build demand tracks the construction cycle and the availability of finance; refurbishment demand tracks the age of the housing stock and household income, both of which move more slowly. A supplier with a position in both channels carries less exposure to a construction slowdown than one selling only into projects.

Smart home technology is the category with most movement on the exhibitor profile. Home automation has shifted from luxury specification to mid-market expectation across the Gulf, driven by falling hardware costs and by residential developers using it as a differentiator. It creates an installation and support requirement that the traditional interiors trade is now building capability to serve.

Hotel equipment appears among Mobedex's categories, overlapping with the Riyadh hospitality cluster running on the same dates. For a Jeddah buyer with a hospitality requirement, the two offer different depths and the choice is straightforward.

Both Jeddah shows run evening hours, 16:00 to 22:00, which suits a trade audience attending after their own working day and reflects a buyer profile of owners and small contractors rather than corporate specifiers.

The organiser is Icon International with KAC. Sponsors named for the combined event include Saudi Red Bricks, Petromin Foton, Reef and, for the China pavilion, CBGG and Zhejiang. Category and sponsor detail is taken from the JIBEX site.

Paints and coatings appear in Mobedex's categories alongside the furniture and flooring, connecting it to the decorative segment of a Gulf coatings market this publication has covered from the manufacturing side.

For suppliers the refurbishment channel is steadier than new build and considerably less visible in published market data, which makes an exhibition one of the few places to read it directly.
